title: Mosaic crochet square
subtitle: Two-colour geometric patterns built from alternating rows with spike stitches
excerpt: Mosaic crochet uses two colours worked in alternating rows, one colour per row, with spike stitches reaching down into the previous same-colour row to pull up the pattern. No yarn is carried across the row — each colour simply works its own rows and the spike stitches create the colour interaction from above.
sourceNotes: Mosaic crochet is a 20th-century development of earlier alternating-row spike stitch techniques documented in Victorian needlework manuals. The mosaic principle appears in Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volume 4 (1889), alternate-row fancy stitch chapter.
heroPrompt: A mosaic crochet square in cream and charcoal DK cotton on a pale linen background, photographed flat from above in soft daylight. Geometric diamond pattern across the surface, 11 cm square.

crochet.gaugeText: Finished mosaic square measures 11 × 11 cm in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook.

chartDefinition.title: Mosaic crochet square
chartDefinition.caption: Rows alternate colour A and colour B. Each colour works only its own rows. Spike stitches reach 2 rows down to bring a contrast stitch to the surface.

glossaryTerms.definition: A spike stitch worked 2 rows down into the previous same-colour row, pulling the current colour down through the previous row's fabric to create a V-shaped colour mark on the surface.

reaches down through the previous row to pull the current colour to the surface, creating the colour interaction.

The square below uses a simple diamond pattern: spike stitches at the corners of a diamond shape on even rows, shifted by one position on odd rows. Once the spike placement is understood, mosaic charts read in the same way as any two-colour stitch map.

attrs.title: Materials for one motif
attrs.body: About 8 g colour A and 8 g colour B in DK-weight cotton. A 4 mm hook. Tapestry needle and scissors.

content.text: Ch 16 in colour A. Row 1: dc in 2nd ch from hook, dc to end. (15 dc.) Fasten off. Row 2 (colour B): join, ch 1. *5 dc, 1 spike (insert hook 2 rows down, draw up long loop to row height), 3 dc, 1 spike, 5 dc.* Turn. Fasten off. Row 3 (colour A): join, ch 1. Work dc with mosaic spikes at shifted positions per chart. Continue alternating colours for 10 rows total, placing spikes per the diamond chart. Fasten off.
For simultaneous two-colour work, try the tapestry crochet square. For a different geometric approach, work the corner-to-corner diamond motif.
